# Cheatsheet Code Snippets

Below are code snippets that will be continuously updated!


## Importing files from online repositories!
1. Are you tired of continuously updating file pathways to match your local file repository? Look no further
```{r}
#Here, I am loading in unabomber texts from an online repository!
test1 <- paste(readLines('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/main/unabomber_manifesto.txt'))

```


## Make a function
2. You can make a function to build unique functions
```{r}
#Here, you can make your own function! The input of the function is a vector which the coder will insert any variable and will get the result due to the function containing select commands
myfunc <- function(x,y) { 

Z <- x+y 

return(Z) 

} 

#You can test myfunc here by simply inputting variables requested by the function

myfunc(3,2)

```


## Gsub (global substitution)
3. gsub is a great function that can remove and replace things you want and don't need  
```{r}
#Just loading in the some text
badtoken <- "Mary had a little lamb"
# The [[:punct:]] observes all punctuation in the token, the " " is to replaces the punctuation, and the "badtoken" is the variable or in other words the content or text you are looking to start cleaning
gonestring <- gsub("[[:punct:]]","",badtoken) 

```


## lowercase
4. if you want lowercase text, use this function!
```{r}
#Loading in a file to mess
badtoken <- "Mary Had A Little Lamb"

#Just a simple code to make the text lowercase!
x <- tolower(badtoken)

print(x)
```


## Splitting strings
5. Another easy code snippet worth mentioning since we are in the realm of NLP. This code is good when you want to tokenize the text you have.
```{r}
#Here is a few lines of code that we can to
gonestring <- "Mary had a little lamb"

splitstring = str_split(gonestring, " ")

```

## A function for replacing words!
7.
```{r}
# Function to replace a word in a target data frame with a replacement word
replace_words <- function(text_vector, replacement_df) {
 # Replace each bad word with its corresponding good word
 for (i in seq_len(nrow(replacement_df))) {
   text_vector <- gsub(
     pattern = replacement_df$mybad[i],
     replacement = replacement_df$mygood[i],
     x = text_vector,
     ignore.case = TRUE
   )
 }
 return(text_vector)
}
```
